evidence_inputs: Node adds 22 lines to imas_codex/units/data_dictionary_unit_aliases.txt: case variants of an existing unit go through @alias (@alias degree = DEG, @alias degC = DegC = oC) so the original unit object and its temperature offset survive; glued digit-exponent and product forms are new units carrying the canonical symbol (KA = 1000 ampere = kA, KV, Mpa, KeV, m2, m3, Pam3); uST = 1e-6 dimensionless. A bare 'n' is deliberately NOT defined because it shadows the nano prefix's parse space and breaks 'count' itself, so the neutron-yield spellings stay unresolved with a reason. New test module tests/units/test_unit_alias_spellings.py (150 lines, 30 tests) proves each spelling against a registry parsed fresh from the alias file; tests/units/collect_dd_unit_strings.py and dd_unit_strings{_base}.txt carry a 487-string DD regression snapshot. Independent review evidence: (1) a live-graph census re-run via GraphClient reproduces census.json exactly - 76 distinct jt-60sa unit strings over 6298 signals, 3954 normalised (64 strings), 2344 unresolved (12 strings); (2) a fresh-process normaliser probe returns zero mismatches - all 16 added spellings normalise to the census's canonical strings, all 11 unresolved spellings return None, analyze_units(KA,A) is compatible at conversion_factor 1000.0 and analyze_units(uST,1) dimensionless at 1e-6, and 20 degC/DegC/oC each convert to 293.15 K in a fresh registry; (3) the negative control reproduces exactly - restoring the self-referential 'DegC = 1 degC = degC' fails test_celsius_spellings_convert_to_kelvin for degC/DegC/oC with RecursionError, 3 failed EXIT=1, and those three ids pass at the head arm.

findings.text: follow-on: consistency - one temperature unit has two canonical spellings depending on the input string. normalize_unit_symbol calls imas_standard_names.canonical_unit first, which formats through its own pint registry and does not load data_dictionary_unit_aliases.txt, so 'DegC' and 'oC' fall through to the alias-loaded registry whose Celsius symbol is the degree sign (°C), while 'degC' and 'degreeC' short-circuit to 'degC'. Reproduced: normalize('DegC') and normalize('oC') both return '°C', normalize('degreeC') returns 'degC'. The conversion is correct (20 -> 293.15 K) and no symbol is redefined, but a downstream consumer comparing canonical strings sees two identities for one unit. The reviewed run discloses this in follow_ons and the test comment says pinning one spelling would pin the wrong layer. Fix: have canonical_unit load the alias file - imas_codex/units/__init__.py and imas_standard_names, outside this node's write paths.

follow-on: fit - the fragment's intro sentence is garbled: 'The alias file now resolves these without claiming a name instead use @alias: a case variant keeps the original offset unit'. The clause 'without claiming a name that pint already owns, and instead uses @alias' has lost its verb and conjunction and closes with a stray colon. The meaning is recoverable from the next sentence, but the paragraph reads as a copy edit left mid-flight. Fix: 'The alias file resolves these without claiming a name pint already owns; a case variant instead uses @alias, which keeps the original offset unit'.

follow-on: evidence - the reviewed manifest leaves baseline_suite and after_suite null, so the added-failure count cannot be read from the record alone and is only recoverable by re-running the arms. This is not a defect in the node's work (the head gate is genuinely green and I reproduced it), but it costs every downstream consumer a base-arm re-run. Fix: fill the manifest's own baseline_suite/after_suite JSON so the added-failure count is readable, as sibling implement nodes do.

follow_ons: resolve the cross-registry canonical-spelling divergence for Celsius (canonical_unit must load the alias file), which the reviewed run correctly scoped out; repair the garbled intro sentence in the evidence fragment; fill the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite/after_suite JSON so the added-failure count is readable without a re-run.

justifications.durability: durability 18: the new module is 30 tests over a fresh-registry fixture plus a checked-in 487-string DD regression snapshot that guards every previously-resolving symbol against a new definition colliding. The negative control is load-bearing and reproduced. Gaps: the unresolved-spelling test asserts None but not the reason string the census carries, so the reasons are run-artifact-only; and the degreeC-vs-DegC divergence is deliberately left untested, so that inconsistency can drift.
justifications.evidence: evidence 19: I reproduced every headline quantity independently. The live-graph census matches census.json to the digit (76/6298/3954/2344 signals, 64/12 strings). A fresh-process probe returns zero mismatches across 16 added and 11 unresolved spellings, KA/A factor 1000, uST dimensionless 1e-6, and 293.15 K for 20 degC/DegC/oC. The negative control reproduces exactly (3 failed, EXIT=1, exactly the ids that pass at head). Both suite arms complete to their summary line with 0 failures. Residual: the reviewed manifest carries no canonical baseline_suite/after_suite JSON, and the Celsius canonical-spelling divergence (degC vs DegC/oC) is a real inconsistency disclosed only as a follow-on.
justifications.fit: fit 19: symbols and filenames are mechanism-named (test_unit_alias_spellings.py, collect_dd_unit_strings.py, dd_unit_strings.txt); no plan, sprint, ticket or version identifiers in code, filenames or comments; the alias-file comment explains the grammars the file must express. Minor defect: the evidence-fragment intro sentence is garbled ('without claiming a name instead use @alias').
justifications.goal_fidelity: goal_fidelity 19: the plan's mechanism is implemented verbatim - spelled forms parsed through the single alias file, a spelling that names no unit listed as unresolved with its count and reason and never guessed, gauge pressure (MPaG) and the neutron-yield family explicitly left unresolved. Delivery is confirmed live and the gate passes. The plan text itself is silent on the cross-registry canonical-spelling interaction the run uncovered.
justifications.reuse: reuse 19: the repair stays in the one file the registry already loads and reuses pint's own offset unit via @alias rather than cloning degC into a second definition, which is the defect the first attempt had. Case variants reuse the canonical unit object; glued forms collapse onto the canonical symbol (KA->kA, Pam3->m^3.Pa). The census script reuses GraphClient.query with bounded DISTINCT reads, and uST reuses the dimensionless base rather than inventing a dimension.
justifications.scope_discipline: scope_discipline 20: the net change sits entirely inside the granted write paths (the alias file, tests/units/, and the declared evidence fragment); no out-of-scope source file, no plan or index edit, no unrelated cleanup; the graph reads the census script performs are bounded DISTINCT queries, not scans.
